analysis.investment_thesis: CarTrade is a digital auto marketplace with improving revenue momentum, but it is one of the worst Magic Formula scores I can assign: earnings yield is only ~1.7% (EBIT ₹152 Cr / EV ₹9,034 Cr) and ROCE is a feeble 7.6% — both metrics fail, and by wide margins. Paying 12× revenue for a platform earning a 7.6% return on capital is precisely the kind of speculative purchase my formula is designed to avoid.
key_strengths: Operating income inflected from -₹133 Cr in FY22 to +₹152 Cr in FY25 — operational turnaround is real and accelerating
Asset-light model: capex is only ₹5 Cr per year, meaning capital employed is minimal and OCF conversion is improving (FY25 OCF ₹171 Cr)
Revenue growing strongly at ~26% CAGR over recent years (₹313 Cr to ₹641 Cr, FY22–FY25) across multi-brand auto platform
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~1.7% is ruinous — the market is capitalizing future growth perfectly, leaving no value buffer
Other income (₹70 Cr) represents ~48% of net profit (₹145 Cr) in FY25 — operating earnings alone barely justify any premium valuation
ROCE of 7.59% is structurally poor; the bloated equity base (₹2,330 Cr, largely from IPO) means the company must grow enormously just to earn an adequate return
red_flags: P/S of 11.98× for an Indian auto marketplace — extraordinarily optimistic pricing
Net profit in FY24 was only ₹20 Cr despite ₹490 Cr revenue — earnings are lumpy and heavily influenced by non-operating items
FII ownership of 64.58% with no disclosed promoter — concentration of foreign capital creates sharp exit risk in a risk-off environment
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict: FAIL on both legs. Earnings yield = ₹152 Cr EBIT / ₹9,034 Cr EV = 1.68% — catastrophically low, less than the risk-free rate. ROCE of 7.6% is not only below my 20% threshold, it barely exceeds the cost of capital. The large equity pile (₹2,330 Cr reserves, largely undeployed IPO capital) is simultaneously suppressing ROCE and distorting ROE (6.24%). Until that capital is either returned or compounded into high-ROIC assets, returns will disappoint.

CarTrade does have the bones of an interesting platform franchise (CarWale, BikeWale, Shriram Automall, OLX autos) and the trajectory is improving. But at ₹8,932 Cr market cap against ₹152 Cr EBIT, you are paying for a perfect five-year execution story that doesn't yet exist. My formula is brutally quantitative — if I cannot compute an acceptable earnings yield today, I don't buy today.
